items.title: 14.5.2 Impact of deforestation on the atmosphere

blocks.text: Deforestation is the purposeful clearing or thinning of forests by humans and is one of the largest issues in global climate: forests absorb greenhouse gases such as CO2 and clean the air for us. Deforestation has a wide range of negative impacts on the environment, including loss of biodiversity, climate change, soil degradation and disruption of the water cycle.

blocks.prompt: How can deforestation affect air quality (exercise Q.2b)?
blocks.explanation: Trees remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis and trap dust and other particles on their leaves; clearing them removes this cleaning, releases the carbon stored in the wood (especially when it is burnt), exposes soil to wind erosion that raises dust, and so leaves the air dirtier and richer in greenhouse gases.

items: Deforestation (clearing or thinning forests) removes the CO2 sink and air cleaner: biodiversity loss, climate change, soil degradation, water-cycle disruption.
